author: Declaration Desk
title: Cabinet clears Rs 11,000 crore incentive to make tunnel borers and excavators at home
dek: The eight-year scheme pays 13% to 8% on extra sales of seven kinds of heavy equipment and five key parts. It comes days after China began requiring export licences for tunnel-boring machines.
body:
The Union Cabinet has approved an Rs 11,000 crore scheme to pay manufacturers for making construction and infrastructure equipment in India, from tunnel-boring machines to excavators and cranes, in an effort to cut imports that the government says meet more than half of demand. Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced the decision after the Cabinet met on Wednesday.

"More than half of it is still imported; this import needs to be reduced so that it is manufactured in India itself," Mr Vaishnaw said of the market for such machinery, which he put at about Rs 1 lakh crore. Another account of his briefing put import dependence at about 45%; reports differ on the exact share.

## What the scheme pays for

The Scheme for Enhancement of Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE) Manufacturing Ecosystem, run by the Ministry of Heavy Industries, covers seven kinds of equipment: tunnel-boring machines, trucks, excavators, cranes, loaders, piling rigs and drilling machines. It also covers five components: engines, transmissions, hydraulic systems, undercarriages and drive systems. Component makers are mostly small and medium firms, Mr Vaishnaw said.

Approved manufacturers will get a sales-linked incentive of 13%, falling to 8%, on the increase in their sales of eligible equipment and parts over five years, according to reports. The scheme runs for eight years from 2026-27: two years to set up factories, incentives paid from 2028-29 to 2032-33, and a final year to settle claims. Up to Rs 375 crore will go to the Automotive Research Association of India, as viability gap funding, to set up a dedicated testing facility for such equipment.

The government expects the scheme to bring in about Rs 21,000 crore of investment, replace Rs 22,500 crore of imports and roughly quadruple exports, according to reports. It did not give a figure for jobs.

## The China angle

The decision lands days after China's Ministry of Commerce brought tunnel-boring machines and their key parts under its export-control regime for dual-use goods, requiring licences from 18 November. Beijing has said the measure is meant to safeguard national security and that compliant applications will be approved, but it has not said which countries count as "sensitive" destinations needing a full licence.

For India, the risk is concrete. Tunnel-boring machines dig metro lines and the rail and road tunnels being built in the Himalaya, including in border areas. A 2020 industry estimate found that nearly 90% of the machines working in India had links to China, either through Chinese makers or foreign brands building them in Chinese factories. In 2025, Germany's ambassador said Chinese customs had held up tunnel-boring machines made by a German company in China for Indian projects. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said this month that India would develop its own machines if China stopped supplying them.

## Background

India's construction equipment market is the world's third largest after China and the US, worth about Rs 97,500 crore in 2024-25 and projected to reach about Rs 2.28 lakh crore by 2029-30 on demand from roads, ports and housing, according to the government's figures. The scheme follows a string of production-linked incentives aimed at Chinese supply chains, including for electronics components and containers.

## What happens next

The Ministry of Heavy Industries will notify the scheme guidelines and open applications. Factories set up in the first two years will be eligible for incentives from 2028-29.
